To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the auroral forms and Pi1B pulsation bursts observed at the auroral latitudes are the signatures of the quasi-oscillatory electron acceleration process that occurs in the upper ionospheric plasma due to the anomalous resistivity caused by the excitation of low-frequency turbulence in a narrow region of the auroral field line.
the auroral zone imaging riometer can be used as an efficient tool to detect localised current filaments.

the field-aligned current intensity estimated from riometer observations during the local current-carry-ing filamentary events can reach the values sufficient to excite the anomalous resistivity regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the auroral zone substorm dynamics using the ground-based observations of riometer absorption, magnetometer data and all-sky images.
the development of new techniques for the analysis of ground-based observations of substorm phenomena.
the study of the ionospheric and magnetospheric processes associated with the auroral substorms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant differences between the auroral zone and polar cap regions.
the field-aligned currents are a major contributor to the energy input to the auroral ionosphere and that they play a major role in auroral dynamics.
the auroral zone field-aligned current density is in the range from 1 to 100 A/m2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the auroral zone ground based observations of the dynamic features of substorm are consistent with the motion up-ward of field-aligned current (FAC) associated with absorption patch moving within the field-of-view (FOV) of the riometer and the estimated FAC intensity is greater than a threshold value that is required for the excitation of low-frequency turbulence in upper ionosphere and the resulting burst-like electron acceleration is responsible for the simultaneously observed auroral form and bursts of Pi 1B pulsations.
we have developed a new method for estimating the intensity of field-aligned currents ( FACS ) in current-carryin g filaments using ground-based riometer observations.
we have demonstrated the existence of a new type of substorm current-carrying filament that can give rise to a burst-like electron acceleration in the auroral field line region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auroral zone ground observations can be used to estimate the field-aligned current intensity associated with current-carrying auroral filaments.

there are two different regimes of the ionospheric conductivity that can be excited in the auroral zone: (1) the quasi-stable regime of the enhanced ionospheric conductivity, which is associated with the FAC intensity exceeding a critical value, and (2) the regime of the anomalous resistivity that can be excited when the ionospheric plasma turbulence is excited.
the current-carrying filamentary structures can play a key role in the development of substorm processes.
